facts.claim: Marriage Act 1961 s 45(2): each party says 'I call upon the persons here present to witness that I, A.B. (or C.D.), take thee, C.D. (or A.B.), to be my lawful wedded wife (or husband, or spouse)', or words to that effect, before a non-religious authorised celebrant and witnesses. Confirmed by the authorised celebrant / AGD.
Marriage Act 1961 s 45(1): ministers of religion use the form recognised by their religious body.

Marriage Act 1961 s 46(1): the civil celebrant says the monitum ('Marriage, according to law in Australia, is the union of 2 people to the exclusion of all others, voluntarily entered into for life.').
AGD: use specific words during the ceremony; NOIM 1 to 18 months ahead; married by an authorised celebrant.
AGD: celebrant, couple and 2 witnesses physically present; certificates signed; lodged within 14 days.
The Act sets minimum words 'or words to that effect'; personal vows, including Bible verses, sit alongside them (our reading, medium). Celebrant confirms final wording.

eBible.org states: 'The World English Bible is in the Public Domain. That means that it is not copyrighted. However, "World English Bible" is a Trademark of eBible.org.' It permits copying, publishing, quoting and reading publicly, and asks only that a changed text not be called the World English Bible. It describes this as the 2020 stable text edition.
facts.publisher: eBible.org (publisher of the World English Bible)
facts.use_note: Translation publisher's own statement. Quote WEB text exactly and label it 'World English Bible'; do not alter wording.

facts.claim: eBible.org KJV page: 'Letters patent issued by King James with no expiration date means that to print this translation in the United Kingdom or import printed copies into the UK, you need permission... This royal decree has no effect outside of the UK, where this work is firmly in the Public Domain.'
facts.use_note: Not an Australian legal authority. No official Australian statement (e.g. Copyright Act 1968, Attorney-General's Department, Australian Copyright Council) on KJV status in Australia was read. One app listing seen in search claims Crown copyright reaches countries with mutual copyright agreements, which conflicts. Treat KJV status in Australia as unconfirmed; see N-01.

facts.claim: Recommendation: quote verses in full only from the World English Bible (public domain per its publisher, F-100). Do not quote the KJV, NIV, ESV, NRSV or other modern translations in full; name them only.
facts.use_note: Research lead recommendation based on F-100 and F-101. The WEB uses 'Yahweh' where many translations say 'LORD' (WEB footnote at Ruth 1:6, Genesis 2:4); couples may prefer their church's translation, which the celebrant or minister can confirm.

facts.claim: "Ruth said, 'Don't urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God. Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May Yahweh do so to me, and more also, if anything but death parts you and me.'"
facts.exact_text: Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God. Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May Yahweh do so to me, and more also, if anything but death parts you and me.
facts.speaker: Ruth, speaking to Naomi, her mother-in-law (Ruth 1:14-15 names Naomi as Ruth's mother-in-law; 1:18 'When Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her').
facts.use_note: The words are spoken by a daughter-in-law to her mother-in-law, not between spouses. State this plainly and neutrally. Verse 16 opens with 'Ruth said,' which is narration, not part of the quote.

facts.exact_text: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.

Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of Yah. Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.
facts.use_note: The WEB titles this book 'Song of Solomon'. WEB footnotes: Sheol is the place of the dead; 'Yah' is a short form of 'Yahweh'. If shortened, mark the cut with an ellipsis.

facts.exact_text: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone? If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
facts.use_note: US spelling 'labor' is in the source; keep it inside the quote.

facts.exact_text: Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart. So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.

He answered, “Haven’t you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female, and said, ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh’? So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.”
facts.use_note: Footnote markers removed. WEB notes 19:4 quotes Genesis 1:27 and 19:5 quotes Genesis 2:24. The speaker is Jesus answering Pharisees (19:3); state context neutrally.

facts.exact_text: What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.

Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud, doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil; doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things. Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Where there are various languages, they will cease. Where there is knowledge, it will be done away with.
facts.use_note: Many ceremonies stop at 'Love never fails.' (8a). If so, cite as 1 Corinthians 13:4-8a.

facts.exact_text: But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.
facts.use_note: The source text contains an em dash after 'remain'. House style bans em dashes; quoting Scripture exactly takes priority. See N-02 for the editor's call.

facts.exact_text: with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love, being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
facts.use_note: Begins mid-sentence (continues 4:1). Quote as printed, lower-case 'with'.

facts.exact_text: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly and gave himself up for her,
facts.use_note: Sentence continues into 5:26; the WEB uses 'assembly' where many translations say 'church'. Verses 5:22-24 directly before it address wives. Present the verse with its reference and no interpretation; couples and their minister choose readings.

facts.exact_text: Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance; bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do. Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.
Beloved, let’s love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God. He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.
There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.
In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to one another; in honor prefer one another,
facts.use_note: Sentence continues into 12:11; end the quote with an ellipsis or full stop marked as shortened.

facts.claim: Our Catholic vows guide: the consent words come from the approved rite and 'vows you write yourselves can't replace them'. 'Your own words belong in the readings, the Universal Prayer, a letter or the reception.' On readings: 'You choose them with your priest, and at least one must speak of marriage. Family or friends who read well may proclaim those before the Gospel, and your story can shape the homily.'
facts.use_note: Internal link target for Catholic couples. Bible verses go in the readings, not in place of the consent.

facts.claim: Our Catholic vows guide (Australia section): the Marriage Act accepts 'any form and ceremony recognised as sufficient' by a minister's church (section 45), so the Catholic consent is the legal vow; the priest does not say the civil monitum (section 46).
facts.use_note: Consistent with F-002 and F-003 (legislation.gov.au). Cite the Act, not our page, for the legal point.

facts.claim: Our traditional vows guide: with traditional vows 'A church, a religious law, or a marriage statute set the words, not the couple.' For Australia it says 'Ministers of recognised religions can use their own rite.' It quotes the Church of England Common Worship service and the Book of Common Prayer (1662) and offers a non-religious, gender-neutral version.
facts.use_note: Internal link for couples who want set religious vow wording rather than verses.

facts.claim: Our how-to-write vows guide: 'A good target is 250 to 300 words, which usually takes about two minutes to read aloud.' It suggests starting with your partner's name and making 3 to 5 specific promises. It does not mention Bible verses or readings.
facts.use_note: Use for weaving one verse into personal vows. Length line conflicts with 'about a minute' elsewhere (N-06).

facts.claim: Our readings guide: 'For a Christian wedding, the Bible offers many passages about love, commitment, marriage and faith. The best known is 1 Corinthians 13, often called the "love chapter". Other possibilities include passages from Ruth, Song of Solomon and Ecclesiastes. If you are having a religious ceremony, check with your church or officiant before you decide. Some traditions have specific requirements about which passages you can use.'
facts.use_note: Main internal link. Note it says 'love chapter', which is our page's wording, not a statistic.

facts.claim: Our readings guide: 'Most readings are around two to three minutes long, and couples usually choose one or two'; readings 'most often come after the opening welcome and before the vows'; 'Your officiant can help you decide where a reading fits best.'

Firecrawl map snippet of our celebrant guide: 'If you or your partner are religious and want to include a bible reading in the ceremony, it's best to check that your celebrant is happy to accommodate.'
facts.use_note: Read from the site map description only, not the full page. Safe as an internal link with this advice; verify full page before quoting.

translation_recommendation: Quote in full only from the World English Bible (public domain, F-100). Label quotes 'World English Bible (WEB)'. Name but do not quote the KJV, NIV, ESV or NRSV. Tell couples their minister or celebrant may ask them to use the church's own translation.

needs.what: Official Australian statement on the KJV's copyright status (Copyright Act 1968, Attorney-General's Department or Australian Copyright Council). Only eBible.org (not a legal authority) says the Crown patent has no effect outside the UK; one app listing claims wider reach. Until sourced, do not quote the KJV in full and do not state its legal status in Australia.
1 Corinthians 13:13 in the WEB contains an em dash ('remain—these three'). Editor to decide: quote exactly (recommended for Scripture) or stop at 13:13 with a comma noted as house style.

Our order-of-service page snippet says a civil ceremony 'must not include anything religious, such as hymns or Bible or Torah readings'. This appears to be the England and Wales (GOV.UK) rule. No Australian official source was read on whether civil celebrants may include Bible readings. Do not state an Australian restriction; say 'check with your celebrant'.
AGD 'Guidelines on the Marriage Act 1961 for authorised celebrants' from an official ag.gov.au URL (carried from funny-vows N-01). Until read, do not quote them.
A real Wedded Wonderland couple or Australian celebrant/minister quote about using a Bible verse in vows, with consent.
House line on vow length: How to Write guide says 250 to 300 words, about two minutes; another page says about a minute. Pick one.
Book name: the brief says 'Song of Songs'; the WEB and our readings page say 'Song of Solomon'. Pick one and give the other in brackets.
